question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cotangent-cosecant identity 

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡x-1={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic identity

$$
1+{csch}^{2}⁡x={coth}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1-{csch}^{4}⁡x}{{csch}^{2}⁡x\,{coth}^{2}⁡x-{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{(1+{csch}^{2}⁡x)(1-{csch}^{2}⁡x)}{-{coth}^{2}⁡x(1-{csch}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1+{csch}^{2}⁡x}{-{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{{coth}^{2}⁡x}{-{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{2}^{4}\text{d}x \\  & =-x{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =-(4-2) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$
